summary: A special lecture on the eve of Dhul Hijjah that links the Prophet Muhammad's SAW sirah to the legacy of Ibrahim AS. Ustaz Azlan covers the merits of the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah, fasting and du'a on the Day of Arafah, the spirit of sacrifice, the Prophet's SAW meeting with Ibrahim AS during the Isra' and Mi'raj and Ibrahim's message to the ummah, then compares the two prophets' calls: challenging an entrenched system, family criticism, imprisonment and expulsion. He explains the farewell sermon on human brotherhood and women's rights, then the crisis of manhood and systems that weaken men, and insists that knowledge must lead to action.
keyPoints: The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah are the days most beloved to Allah for righteous deeds, outdone only by martyrdom of one who goes out with life and wealth.
Fasting on Arafah expiates the sins of the previous year and the coming year, and du'a on Arafah is the best du'a.
The Prophet SAW met Ibrahim AS on the Isra' and Mi'raj; Ibrahim sent greetings to the ummah and said Paradise has fragrant soil and is cultivated by dhikr.
The Prophet SAW described himself as the answer to his father Ibrahim's prayer and the glad tiding of Jesus.
Both prophets challenged an entrenched idol system and both faced criticism from family and expulsion.
The farewell sermon stressed that all humans come from Adam, no race is superior except by taqwa, and women have rights.
Religious knowledge must be followed by action, starting with putting our own families right.

Keeper of the house of idols; Ibrahim addressed him gently.

The Prophet SAW pleaded with him to say the shahadah until the end.

lessons.title: Welcome what is promised as thanks
lessons.body: Celebrating Dhul Hijjah's merits by increasing worship is an expression of gratitude.

lessons.title: Fast Arafah if you are not on Hajj
lessons.body: A very good sunnah, and do not make obligatory what is not.

lessons.title: Plan your du'a on Arafah
lessons.body: Divide the time into slots for yourself, family and the ummah, balancing this world and the next.

lessons.title: Sacrifice until it is hard
lessons.body: Give something you love enough to feel the sacrifice, not a little out of a lot.

lessons.title: Fast from distractions
lessons.body: Try ten days without social media and a ceasefire from arguments.

lessons.title: Worship is not content
lessons.body: Hajj and umrah should not become content, losing the focus of worship.

lessons.title: State the truth without hatred
lessons.body: Ibrahim and Muhammad did not answer with curses and kept seeking forgiveness for family.

lessons.title: Knowledge must be followed by action
lessons.body: The main problem is not lack of knowledge but lack of courage to take the first step.

lessons.title: Human brotherhood
lessons.body: No race is above another, and refugees deserve compassion, not mockery.

lessons.title: Protect women and raise strong men
lessons.body: Strong men protect, not abuse, women; systems that weaken men must be resisted.

lessons.title: The ummah's strength needs many roles
lessons.body: Not lectures alone: it needs principled entrepreneurs, politicians and educators, and balance in family life.

lessons.title: Choose your fight
lessons.body: Each person picks their own arena and begins with their family and with wisdom.

dalil.context: Linked to the mindset of making the most of the first ten days.
dalil.translation: No righteous deed is more beloved to Allah than in these days; the companions asked, 'Not even jihad?' He said, 'Not even jihad, except a man who goes out with his life and wealth and returns with nothing.'

dalil.context: Mentioned as an excellent sunnah for those not at Arafah.
dalil.translation: Fasting on the Day of Arafah, I hope from Allah that it expiates the previous year and the coming year.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the hadith is said to be narrated by Imam Tirmidhi.
dalil.translation: The best du'a is the du'a on the Day of Arafah.

dalil.context: Combined from several narrations; the part on conveying greetings is from Tirmidhi.
dalil.translation: I entered and saw Ibrahim; he welcomed me with 'welcome, righteous prophet and righteous son,' and said, 'Convey my greetings to your ummah.'

dalil.context: Ibrahim's message to the Prophet's SAW ummah.
dalil.translation: Tell them that Paradise has fragrant soil and fresh water, it is a wide plain whose plants are Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah and Allahu Akbar.

dalil.context: The Prophet's SAW answer when asked to tell about himself.
dalil.translation: I am the answer to my father Ibrahim's prayer and the glad tiding of Jesus.

dalil.context: Gathered from several narrations in the Arafah sermon.
dalil.translation: O people, your Lord is one and your father is one; you are all from Adam and Adam is from dust; no Arab is above a non-Arab, nor white above black, except by taqwa.

dalil.context: The Prophet's SAW message in a society that denied women rights.
dalil.translation: You have rights over your women and they have rights over you; be good to them, for they are like captives in your hands; fear Allah regarding women.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains men's responsibility to protect the women in their lives.
dalil.translation: The dayyuth will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.

dalil.context: Ibrahim's prayer for a messenger from among them who recites the verses, teaches the book and wisdom, and purifies their souls.
dalil.translation: Our Lord, make a messenger of their own rise up from among them, to recite Your revelations to them, teach them the Scripture and wisdom, and purify them: You are the Mighty, the Wise.’

dalil.context: The comprehensive du'a that balances this world and the next. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: others pray, ‘Our Lord, give us good in this world and in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire.’

dalil.context: People were made into nations to know one another, and the most honoured is the most righteous. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: People, We created you all from a single man and a single woman, and made you into races and tribes so that you should recognize one another. In God’s eyes, the most honoured of you are the ones most mindful of Him: God is all knowing, all aware.

dalil.context: Surah Tabbat came down when Abu Lahab insulted the Prophet SAW on Mount Safa. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined! May he be ruined too!

dalil.context: Allah describes Ibrahim as a model. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: You have a good example in Abraham and his companions, when they said to their people, ‘We disown you and what you worship besides God! We renounce you! Until you believe in God alone, the enmity and hatred that has arisen between us will endure!’––except when Abraham said to his father, ‘I will pray for forgiveness for you though I cannot protect you from God’––[they prayed] ‘Lord, we have put our trust in You; we turn to You; You are our final destination.

dalil.context: Ibrahim promised to keep asking forgiveness for his father. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Abraham said, ‘Peace be with you: I will beg my Lord to forgive you- He is always gracious to me-
